cards.text: In the tenth year, on the twelfth day of the tenth month, the word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel the prophet. God calls him "Son of man" and hands him a new assignment. He's to set his face against Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and prophesy against him.

cards.question: God tells Ezekiel to prophesy against Pharaoh and against all ___.

cards.text: Then God speaks straight to Pharaoh. He says He is against him, and He calls him a great monster who lies among his rivers. A river monster, friend. To his FACE.

cards.question: The great monster lying among his rivers has a brag about the Nile. What does Pharaoh say?

answers.text: The Nile is mine and I made it myself
The Nile was handed to me by my gods
The Nile will flow forever just for me

cards.text: So God says He'll put hooks in Pharaoh's jaws and haul him up out of his rivers. Pharaoh thinks he owns the river. Turns out God's the one holding the line.

cards.question: As God hauls the river monster up out of his rivers, what comes up clinging to his scales?

cards.text: God says He'll leave him in the desert with all those fish, to fall on the open field. A river monster dropped in the DESERT, baker. I know that move: kitchen counter to the back of a junk drawer, no warning.

cards.question: After the river monster falls on the open field, he'll be gathered up for a proper burial.
God says He's given Pharaoh as food to the beasts and the birds. When that happens, what will all the people of Egypt know?

answers.text: That their gods have left them
That their king has run away

cards.text: Then God brings up the house of Israel, and how they'd been leaning on Egypt. He has a picture for what Egypt was to them: a staff.

cards.question: God says Egypt was only a staff of ___ to the house of Israel.
When Israel leaned on Egypt, that staff of reeds, what happened?

answers.text: It broke and their backs were wrenched
It held but bent down low
It sank into the soft mud

cards.text: They grabbed it, and it splintered and tore their shoulders. They leaned on it, and it broke. That's the cheap office chair at work, friend. You lean back in it ONCE.

cards.question: Because of all this, God says He will bring a sword against Egypt and cut off man and beast.

cards.text: God says, "The land of Egypt will become a desolate wasteland. Then they will know that I am the LORD."

cards.question: God says He's against Pharaoh, and against his rivers too. Why?

answers.text: Pharaoh said the Nile was his and he made it
Pharaoh dammed the Nile to keep Israel out
Pharaoh let the Nile run dry from neglect

cards.text: So God will turn Egypt into a ruin from Migdol to Syene, as far as the border of Cush. Pharaoh bragged about that river twice, and God heard him BOTH times.

cards.question: No foot of man or beast will pass through, and Egypt will be uninhabited for ___ years.
During those forty years, the Egyptians stay together in their own land.

cards.text: But God's not done talking about Egypt. He looks ahead to the end of those forty years.

cards.question: When the forty years are up, what does God say He'll do with the scattered Egyptians?

answers.text: Gather them back from the nations

cards.text: God says He'll restore Egypt from captivity and bring them back to the land of Pathros, the land of their origin. Home again, after forty years away.

cards.question: Back in Pathros, God says Egypt will be a ___ kingdom.
Someday Egypt will rise up again and rule over the nations.

cards.text: God says He'll diminish Egypt so it never again exalts itself above the nations. Friend, I know that fall. One day you're the star of the counter, the next day you're under a takeout menu.

cards.question: God says Egypt will never again be something Israel puts its trust in. Instead, what will Egypt remind the house of Israel of?

answers.text: Their iniquity in turning to Egypt
Their long years as slaves in Egypt
Their escape across the Red Sea

cards.text: That's the end of the first message. Then the date jumps to the twenty-seventh year, on the first day of the first month, and the word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel again.

God tells him Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, worked his army hard against Tyre. Every head was made bald and every shoulder made raw. That's not overtime, baker. That's overtime that took your HAIR.

cards.question: After all that hard labor against Tyre, Nebuchadnezzar and his army got paid well by Tyre.

cards.text: Bald heads. Raw shoulders. Zero wages. So the Lord GOD steps in with a payday.

cards.question: God gives the land of ___ to Nebuchadnezzar, and its plunder will be the ___ for his army.
Why does God say He gives Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar as the reward for his labor?

answers.text: Because the labor was done for God
Because Babylon begged God for it

cards.text: Then, at the very end, God turns to His own people, the house of Israel. Something new is coming for them in that day.

cards.question: In that day, God says He will cause a ___ to sprout for the house of Israel.
God also says He will open Ezekiel's mouth to speak among the house of Israel.

cards.text: And God closes with that line one more time: "Then they will know that I am the LORD." Pharaoh wanted his name on the Nile. God made sure the last word belongs to Him.

findings.problem: Card 1 already calls Pharaoh 'king of Egypt' and says Ezekiel prophesies against him. That gives away 'Egypt' for the blank 'against all ___' and rules out Assyria and Edom before the baker picks.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card says 'God speaks straight to Pharaoh' and adds 'To his FACE.' In Ezekiel 29:3, God tells Ezekiel, 'Speak to him and tell him that this is what the Lord GOD says.' The message goes through Ezekiel, so the text shows God is not speaking straight to Pharaoh.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The joke says Papa Dorin went from the kitchen counter to the junk drawer with 'no warning.' His backstory says he saw it coming: he looked at each new box sideways because 'He knew how this story went. It was only a matter of time.' The joke changes his backstory.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: Card 12 already revealed that the staff broke and wrenched Israel's backs when they leaned on it. This story card retells that ('They leaned on it, and it broke') and moves the 'splintered' detail after the leaning, so it works mostly as a recap.

The card says 'Pharaoh bragged about that river twice.' The text never says Pharaoh bragged twice. God quotes the brag twice (Ezekiel 29:3 and 29:9), and the two quotes use different wording ('I made it myself' and 'I made it').

rule.text: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: Card 5 already asked whether Egypt will rule over the nations again. This story card retells the same verse 15 idea ('diminish Egypt so it never again exalts itself above the nations'), so it reads as a recap and doesn't move the passage forward.
The joke says 'under a takeout menu' as a drawer detail, but the line doesn't say the menu was in the junk drawer. A baker may not catch what it means.

rule.text: The drawer's small details, like the batteries, the key or the coupon, only come up when the line says what they are, like "the dead batteries I shared that drawer with."

findings.problem: The setup card says 'Zero wages' and 'payday' just before card 12, which asks the baker to fill in 'wages' as the second blank. That gives the answer away. The card also mostly repeats card 9 and card 10 ('Bald heads. Raw shoulders. Zero wages.').

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The blank 'cause a ___ to sprout' asks for the exact word 'horn,' and card 14 gives no context to reason from ('Something new is coming for them'). It tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning they can work out.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
